headline_marked: [[ChatGPT now guesses your age]] and restricts users under 18 by default
headline: ChatGPT now guesses your age and restricts users under 18 by default
summary: OpenAI has rolled out an age prediction system that infers user age from behavior, potentially placing adults into a restricted "ChatGPT for Teens" experience. This system can override a user's stated birthdate.
details: OpenAI has rolled out an age prediction system for ChatGPT, which quietly guesses if a user is under 18. If identified as a minor, accounts are automatically switched to a restricted 'ChatGPT for Teens' version, without explicit user consent. This rollout began on August 18.

The age prediction mechanism is behavioral, analyzing 'general topics you talk about, the times of day you use ChatGPT, how and when your account is used, and how long your account has existed.' OpenAI admits the system is imperfect and can misclassify users.

ChatGPT for Teens includes stronger safety defaults, reducing sensitive content like graphic violence, risky challenges, or romantic/violent roleplay. It also features break reminders and product cues, and will not show ads, unlike the standard ChatGPT experience.

Crucially, this system can override a user's previously provided date of birth. OpenAI states that 'no system is perfect' and that some adults will be incorrectly placed into the teen experience, despite their actual age.

Users misclassified as minors can exit the restricted experience by verifying their age through a third-party service called Persona. This process may require a live selfie, a government ID, or both, depending on the user's country.

headline_marked: [[GLM-5.3-Flash from Z.ai]] offers 10x cost savings over top AI models
headline: GLM-5.3-Flash from Z.ai offers 10x cost savings over top AI models
summary: The model, secretly tested as 'Ox Alpha', delivers comparable intelligence to leading US models at a fraction of the cost, running entirely on Chinese infrastructure.
details: A week ago, a mystery model named Ox Alpha appeared on OpenRouter, quickly gaining traction among hobbyists and indie developers for its free access and quiet performance. It processed trillions of tokens daily, sparking widespread speculation about its origin and the infrastructure supporting it.

On August 26, Z.ai officially claimed the model, revealing it as GLM-5.3-Flash. The surprise extended beyond its capabilities to its underlying infrastructure: it is served entirely on Chinese chips and infrastructure. The model is open-weight (MIT license), with inference hosted by Z.ai, GMI Cloud, Cloudflare, and other US-based providers.

Artificial Analysis placed GLM-5.3-Flash at 57 on its intelligence-versus-cost chart, costing about nine cents per task. This compares to a US mid-tier model like GPT-5.6 Sol at 59 intelligence points for 67 cents, or Grok 4.6 at 61 points for 94 cents. This means GLM-5.3-Flash offers a 7x to 10x cost advantage for comparable intelligence.

American enterprises are already facing significant cost pressures from AI usage. Uber's CTO, Praveen Neppalli Naga, reported blowing through the company's 2026 coding budget in just four months, leading to a $1,500-per-person-per-tool cap. While AI tools are useful, the high costs are prompting companies to re-evaluate their spending.

Chinese model makers like Zhipu, Qwen, and DeepSeek are increasingly challenging SOTA labs and driving down costs. Chinese models surpassed US token share on OpenRouter in early June, with indie developers now heavily favoring cost-effective options like GLM Flash and DeepSeek Flash. This shift forces companies to reconsider expensive subscriptions if pay-as-you-go alternatives become significantly cheaper.

Organizations must now optimize AI usage by categorizing tasks across different intelligence tiers. For most coding and agentic work (around 50% of volume), mid-tier models like GLM-5.3-Flash offer excellent value. Top-tier models like Fable and Opus should be reserved for critical, complex tasks where every point of intelligence matters, likely comprising only 5% of total task volume.
